translation_notes: Identity translation: the query is assembled from two runtime pieces, neither of which is a term. `self._filter` (real shape, see driver.py: `FILTER STRSTARTS(STR(?g), "prefix")`, set in __init__ from a constructor argument) is spliced straight after the `GRAPH ?g { ... }` block -- an opaque SPARQL FILTER fragment, not a value: s{ }'s {expr} only stands where a term may stand, and there is no island for 'a filter clause held in a variable'.

When `triple` is given, `inner_where = "%s %s %s" % tuple(i.n3() for i in triple)` builds a WHOLE triple pattern from data received as an argument -- the same limit INSTRUCTIONS.md SS2 notes for -{ }/m{ } (a WRITTEN pattern only, never one received as data), here on rdflib's own query engine rather than a BGP island. Subject, predicate and object all vary independently across callers, so there is no fixed term slot to interpolate even after the fact.

The source's own comment shows the author already considered and rejected the term-interpolation shape this stratum expects: 'the right thing to do would be initBindings[...] but this would not work with Virtuoso'. Same limit, same shape, as the sibling city-knowledge-graphs/python-2023 checkEntailment region in this stratum.

contexts(self, triple=None) is a generator on PrefixConjunctiveView (a ConjunctiveGraph subclass); driver.py restores only the three attributes it reads (store, _whole, _filter) as a minimal stand-in class, not the ktbs/rdfrest resource machinery its sibling region (lib/ktbs/engine/trace.py post_graph) needed -- that one is excluded, this one is fully executable.
